results.title: Poddle: Swing your phone, play pickleball on any computer! | Product Hunt
results.content:
To move around the court, your webcam tracks where you stand. The video never leaves your computer. No camera? The game runs you to the ball automatically, like Wii Sports tennis, so you just swing.  
  
Early into the project, I added phone support for ease of testing. It ended up staying, though, since everyone already has one, and the time to play was so much faster than AirPods.  
  
You can also play Matt the bot at various difficulties, play friends online, earn trophies, run a knockout tournament, or watch live matches.  
  
Poddle is free, and you don't need an account unless you’re someone who likes progression and tracking your stats. Any feedback on how the swing feels and on potential future features is greatly appreciated. Have fun! 🥒 [...] Poddle

Hey Product Hunt, I'm Daniel, and this is my first launch! 😁  
  
Poddle started as a last-minute hackathon idea. AirPods have motion sensors, so we wondered if one could work as a pickleball paddle, in Wii Sports fashion. And it worked better than we expected! We didn't win anything, but I kept building it anyway out of love for the idea of the project, and I've been having tons of fun with my friends at university clubs playing and testing it ever since.  
  
Most of my time went into making the swing feel right. A motion sensor knows how your hand turns, not where it is, so the game reads the swing itself: speed and reach set the power, direction aims it, a scoop lobs it, and a wrist cut adds spin.

results.title: Ohio Trucking Permits and Registrations
results.content:
Past the general permits Ohio keeps a long bench of special ones: construction equipment, farm equipment, manufactured building, marina and boat permits that each run a year; steel or aluminum coil permits that treat three or fewer coils as a nondivisible load; an international sealed container permit for sealed export freight; a regional heavy hauling permit the director must issue on written application; and the Michigan legal permit, which lets an overweight truck run prescribed routes between three border counties and the Michigan line at Michigan weight law.

Our Ohio oversize and overweight page carries the full fee schedule, escort thresholds, curfews and the cost deposit Ohio uses in place of a superload tier.

## Curfews and moving bans [...] Ohio is not one of the five weight-distance states. An Ohio-based carrier files IFTA quarterly through OH|TAX eServices and owes no separate per-mile highway use tax to Ohio. The Ohio Department of Taxation's own IFTA pamphlet lists the states with an additional mileage tax, and Ohio is not among them; the list it gives is Kentucky, Arkansas, New Mexico, Oregon, Idaho, New York and Connecticut.

## The Ohio permit system

## The permit office and the hauling permit system [...] The word superload does not appear in Ohio Adm.Code Chapter 5501:2-1. The practical break is 120,000 pounds gross vehicle weight, above which the overweight surcharge adds four cents per ton over sixty tons per mile travelled. Where a move needs special traffic control or special engineering analysis, the applicant deposits the department's estimated direct costs in advance and reimburses the actual cost, which is what Ohio uses in place of a named superload review tier.

### The Michigan legal permit, a border-county-only overweight credentialOhio Administrative Code Rule 5501:2-1-01Verified Jul 25, 2026
